exec.recommended_action_label: AM-led recovery or refund within 7 days

summary_paragraphs: Be Beauty Studio is a single-location waxing and brow studio in Fairfield, CT, operated by Cristina Sousa. The account paid for Discovery Agent on 2026-05-07 at $600 per quarter ($200/month equivalent). The customer self-onboarded via the Zoca application; a Zoca account executive then placed two outbound phone calls on the same day before payment, both of which the rep used for scheduling and tech-coordination rather than ICP qualification.

Applied against the canonical Module 02 ICP framework, the account fails Step 1.2 (six-month lead-prediction gate) automatically. The model output predicted_6_month_leads = 26 sits below the 30-lead Non-ICP floor confirmed by Sales Ops. Module 02's binary rule applies: any single failure in Step 1 or Step 2 = Not ICP. The booking-platform gate (Step 1.3) does pass — Be Beauty Studio is on GlossGenius — but a Step-1.3 pass cannot rescue a Step-1.2 automatic fail.

Reinforcing flags compound the verdict. Module 02 names a < 20 review-count disqualifier; Be Beauty Studio sits at 13 reviews at onboarding (despite an exceptional 5.00 average). Google Business Profile (GBP) opening-date verification is currently a data gap — the entity is not synced to gbp.locations, and the gbp.reviews table is not configured in the validator. The single-location-plus-solo Rule B (annual revenue ≥ $100K) was never asked at the point of sale. Six support tickets exist in the 30-day window as of day 1 of the customer's relationship with Zoca.

Cristina's verbatim words on the discovery call were: "I don't love the app… I want to see how it works and the costs for…" The rep promised a 15-minute Google Meet covering product walk-through, lead prediction, and a business analysis. The Google Meet content is not captured in any data source, so the substantive demo is not auditable. A 74-second outbound phone call at 22:30 UTC shows the rep helping Cristina rejoin the meeting after a connection issue. Cristina paid 60 minutes after the rejoin call. The customer paid based on expectations the rep set, not on auditable value the rep delivered.

The Module 02 doctrine for this profile is unambiguous: under the "BE HONEST. FULL STOP." value, the account manager (Shruti Sinha) must contact Cristina within 7 days, run the qualification the AE skipped, and either recover the account cleanly (verified revenue ≥ $100K and a real lead pipeline that beats the model projection of 26) or issue a refund and set a re-entry trigger. Given that the lead-prediction figure is in the auto-fail tier, a refund is the most likely Module-02-correct outcome.
exec.net_retention_picture: Account does not meet ICP threshold under Module 02. Recommended action is AM-led requalification within 7 days, followed by retain (if Rule B and lead-pipeline checks confirm) or refund within 14 days.
exec.likely_outcome: refund and re-entry trigger. The auto-fail tier on Step 1.2 is the decisive gate; the booking-platform pass on Step 1.3 cannot rescue it.

section3_risks.intro: This register catalogues the residual risks associated with allowing this account to remain on Discovery without remediation.

risks.driver_mitigation: Lead-prediction in auto-fail tier; demo content not delivered; quarterly billing has no contractual lock. Mitigation: AM-led requalification + refund-or-recover by day 14.

Customer paid $600 USD. If churn occurs at day 90, the at-risk amount is the $600 invoice plus net cost-to-serve (estimated at multiples of the invoice for at-onboarding spend). Mitigation: refund within 14 days bounds the exposure to $600 plus cost-to-serve already incurred.

AE never asked Step-1.1 (device), Step-1.3 (platform — would have passed), Step-2 row, or Rule B (revenue). Pattern suggests a self-serve checkout path that bypasses ICP qualification. Mitigation: Section 7 organisational recommendations.

risks.risk: Brand / reputation if customer churns publicly
risks.driver_mitigation: Customer's statement before payment — "I don't love the app" — combined with set-but-unauditable demo expectations indicates risk of negative review or social-media post if Day-30 outcomes do not meet promises.

The GlossGenius URL on file is bebeautybytina.glossgenius.com (suggests a different operator), and the Instagram/Facebook handles linked to the entity are emilys.nails.spa / emilysnails.spa. The validator cannot rule out cross-entity data conflation. Mitigation: AM identity verification + data-engineering review.

Module 02 disqualifies GBPs less than approximately 3 months old. Be Beauty Studio is not present in the gbp.locations CSV (zero matches across 991 entities). The gbp.reviews fallback method is not currently configured. Mitigation: AM call closes; data-engineering pipeline gap to be addressed.

Module 02 carve-out list (threading-only, nails-only, eyelash-only, braiders) does not literally include waxing-only, but the cost-to-serve / LTV reasoning that justifies the existing carve-outs applies with similar force. Future similar accounts will hit the same edge.

Underlying inputs: 31 days of pre-onboard GBP signal — search clicks 81, map clicks 54 (sum = 135 profile clicks), plus 27 direction requests, 14 website clicks, 1 call click.

The validator cannot rule out cross-entity data conflation. The AM should verify the GlossGenius account is operated by Cristina before treating this as a confirmed pass.

section4_framework.step1_conclusion: Cannot pass. Step 1.2 is an automatic fail under the tier rule.
step2_row_evidence: Evidence supporting single-location: one entity in BaseSheet; billing address 166 Halley Avenue, Fairfield, CT 06825 (single address).

Evidence supporting solo (suggestive, not definitive): personal Gmail used for Chargebee billing rather than a business domain; Apple Pay — a consumer-grade payment instrument; self-serve checkout via the Zoca application with no AE involvement at the point of decision; the residential billing address is typical of home-based studios; no employee references in any captured communication. A counter-signal: the public Facebook page reportedly uses "we / team" language, which could be marketing or could indicate help. Not decisive.

step2.rule: Rule A — must NOT be in the four single-location carve-outs (threading-only, nails-only, eyelash-only, braiders)
step2.evidence: Waxing-only is not literally in the carve-out list. However, the cost-to-serve / LTV economics that justify the existing carve-outs apply to waxing-only single-location with similar force. This is a Sales Ops policy question and is flagged in Section 7 organisational recommendations.

Revenue was not asked at the point of sale. No revenue evidence is available in any captured source. The residential billing address (166 Halley Avenue), sole-proprietor operating profile (personal Gmail, Apple Pay, self-serve checkout), and a small lifetime review base (13) are circumstantial signals consistent with a sub-$100K operation, but cannot substitute for direct verification. The AM call must close.

section4_framework.summary_takeaway: any single failure in Step 1 OR Step 2 = Not ICP. Step 1.2 is the decisive failure. The booking-platform pass cannot rescue the gate.
section4_framework.one_line_blockquote: Predicted_6_month_leads = 26 places Be Beauty Studio under the 30-lead Non-ICP floor — a Step-1 hard fail by itself. Reinforced by 13 < 20 reviews and an unverifiable GBP age. The booking-platform pass and exceptional rating are real positives but cannot rescue a Step-1 fail under Module 02.

blocks.text: Call A — 16:55:58 UTC, 168 seconds (discovery call)

"As a part of the process, what we do is that we actually provide you with a Google Meet call. It will hardly take us 15 minutes... we'll show you each and everything. We'll also do a lead prediction for you. Entire business analysis for you."
Scope-setting call. No Step-1 questions asked: device check, booking platform check, lead-prediction surfacing from BaseSheet. A Google Meet was scheduled for 5:30 PM Eastern (21:30 UTC nominal).
Call B — 22:30:23 UTC, 74 seconds (tech-coordination phone call)

"Hello? Hello. Hi, Christina. I think the problem has resolved now. You can just join in again... I tried a few times. I was like, maybe they're busy in another call. Let me wait a little bit... I see you over there. Just allow me a second. I'll admit you. Hi, Christina. nice to meet you..."

This 74-second exchange was a phone call helping Cristina rejoin the Google Meet after a connection issue. The Google Meet itself took place after the 22:30 UTC rejoin and is the actual demo session. The Google Meet content is NOT captured in available data sources — Fireflies search by participant email, business name, and date range returns zero indexed transcripts. The demo's substance and duration are not auditable.
Promised vs. delivered

rows: "15-minute Google Meet to help you understand what exactly we offer"
Not auditable — no Fireflies transcript captured. The 22:30 UTC phone call (74 s) was tech-coordination only.
"How exactly we are going to get you more customers on the full price of the service"

section6_actions.intro: Five actions are required to bring this account into Module-02 compliance or to terminate it cleanly with a refund and a re-entry trigger.

actions.action: Schedule and run a 30-minute requalification call with Cristina. Cover Step 1.1 (device), Step 1.3 (platform — confirm GlossGenius identity match), Step 2 row, Rule B (revenue), GBP opening date, and PMU services question.
actions.success_criterion: Call completed; all six gaps closed; outcome documented in HubSpot.

actions.action: Investigate the six open tickets (BaseSheet open_tickets_last_30_days = 6). Categorise by issue type and resolve.
actions.success_criterion: All tickets resolved or have an owner with ETA.

actions.action: Branch on outcome of A1. (a) If revenue ≥ $100K AND a real lead pipeline beats the 26-lead model projection, retain. Reset expectations and deliver the demo content that was promised. (b) If revenue is below $100K and customer is solo, refund and set re-entry trigger per Module 02 doctrine.
actions.success_criterion: Decision documented; refund issued or onboarding plan committed.

actions.action: Document the audit trail for this account in HubSpot, including AE qualification gaps, AM resolution, and final decision (retain / refund).
actions.success_criterion: HubSpot record exists with full notes.

actions.action: Verify the GlossGenius account at bebeautybytina.glossgenius.com is operated by Cristina Sousa. If not, escalate to data-engineering for entity-record correction.
actions.success_criterion: Identity confirmed; data record corrected if needed.

section6_actions.am_script: "Cristina, I want to be straight with you. We took your payment yesterday but we owe you the actual qualification call we never ran. Couple of quick scope questions before we set anything up: laptop or iPad at the studio day-to-day? Just you for now, or anyone helping? And revenue-wise — under $100K, low six figures, more? And how long has your Google Business Profile been live?"
branch_paragraphs: Branch on Cristina's answers as documented in Action A3.

section7_systemic.intro: This account exposes systemic gaps that are likely to recur. Eight recommendations are proposed; ownership and priority are assigned.

recommendations.recommendation: Add an automated pre-checkout ICP qualification gate for self-serve onboarding flows. Block self-serve checkout when predicted_6_month_leads is in the auto-fail tier.
recommendations.rationale: This account would have been blocked at the gate; the AE never had a chance to qualify.

recommendations.recommendation: Mandate a Step-1 / Step-2 qualification checklist on every AE-led discovery call before payment. Embed as a HubSpot deal-stage requirement.
recommendations.rationale: Skipped qualification is the failure mode that produced this account.

recommendations.recommendation: Resolve the gbp.locations sync gap. Investigate why entity 9d830e96-…ec34 is not present in the 991-entity table; ensure newly onboarded entities are synced.
recommendations.rationale: GBP age is a Module 02 disqualifier; current data gap means it cannot be enforced.

recommendations.recommendation: Configure the gbp.reviews fallback method in the Payment Validator to verify GBP age via earliest-review timestamp when gbp.locations is missing.
recommendations.rationale: Provides defence-in-depth on the GBP-age disqualifier.

recommendations.recommendation: Close the question: should waxing-only single-location be added to the four named carve-outs in Module 02? Sales Ops review and decision.
recommendations.rationale: Edge case will recur. Borderline-case reasoning today should become explicit policy.

recommendations.recommendation: Tighten Fireflies transcript indexing for Google Meet demos so post-payment audit can verify what was demonstrated and promised.
recommendations.rationale: Demo content for this account is not auditable. Pattern likely affects other accounts.

recommendations.recommendation: Distinguish self-serve from AE-sourced lead source in BaseSheet and HubSpot. Update lead_source labelling logic — self-onboard followed by reactive AE call should not be tagged "Outbound."
recommendations.rationale: Current label is misleading; affects retention modelling and channel attribution.

recommendations.recommendation: Resolve the entity-record conflation pattern (mismatched URL/social handles for a single entity). Audit similar cases.
recommendations.rationale: Cross-entity data quality issue undermines all downstream decisions.

methodology_paragraphs: This review was produced by the Zoca Payment Validator pipeline, which runs every 30 minutes and produces a structured analysis for each new Discovery first-payment customer. The pipeline is fully automated and follows a deterministic data-fetching stage followed by a structured LLM evaluation against the canonical Module 02 prompt.

Step 1 of the pipeline — deterministic data fetching — pulled the Chargebee customer record, located the matching Stripe customer by email, validated the timestamp parity, and confirmed first-ever-subscription status at the Chargebee customer-id level. Step 2 — enrichment — pulled the BaseSheet entity record, all five communications channels (App Chat, Email, Phone Calls, SMS, Video) filtered to entity_id with the 90-day window before payment, the booking-platform CSV, the business-opening-date CSV, the review-metrics CSV, the Fireflies transcript index, and the HubSpot CRM record. Step 3 — evaluation — applied the Module 02 prompt to the bundled evidence.

The validator does not invent data. Where a data source is unavailable for an entity, the analysis explicitly marks the field as a data gap rather than guessing. All claims in this report are footnoted to a specific data source — the source attribution is the first row of every per-section banner and is repeated inline where evidence is quoted.

Subjective judgements (for example, the inference of single-location-plus-solo from residential billing address + personal Gmail + Apple Pay) are explicitly labelled as best-evidence reads rather than confirmed facts. Confirmed facts use the source-cited evidence directly.
